title: IACW: Intent-Aware Controllable Watermarking for Scalable Authorial Intent Attribution
claim: Binary detectors lump AI-polished and AI-generated text together; intent-aware attribution separates anchored editing from unanchored generation.
layout: 2 stacked rows, left-to-right flow, color-coded editing vs generation lanes
description: Two horizontal lanes separated by dashed lines. The top lane is a blue 'Editing Intent (Anchored)' lane. A user icon gives an anchor text with a polish prompt, which goes through a neural-net LLM icon to Output y1. Output y1 is text with red edited words. A 'From LLM / From User' provenance tag sits below it. Two arrows leave the output. A gray arrow goes to a 'Binary Detector' box labeled 'AI Generated'. A blue arrow goes to 'IACW (Ours)', labeled 'Editing (AI-assisted)'. The bottom lane is green and labeled 'Generation Intent (No anchored)'. It has the same structure, with an empty anchor X=∅ and a 'write about climate change' prompt. The binary detector again says 'AI Generated', with a red warning 'Same as polishing'. The green IACW arrow gives 'Generation (AI-authored)'. Gray vs. colored arrows mark the contrast.
caption: The paradigm shift from post-hoc detection to proactive
abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) integrate into writing workflows, precise governance requires distinguishing ''how AI participated'' rather than merely ''whether AI was used.'' Traditional binary detection often misclassifies ``AI-polished'' content as generated, creating fairness risks. We propose shifting from passive post-hoc detection to active intent attribution, focusing on the distinction between Editing (source-anchored) and Generation (unanchored). We introduce \textbf{IACW-Instruct}, a corpus of diverse editing operations constructed via a Director--Actor--Judge pipeline to enable systematic evaluation. Building on this benchmark, we propose \textbf{Intent-Aware Controllable Watermarking (IACW)}, featuring intent-adaptive entropy gating for semantically lossless embedding. Experiments show that IACW achieves 95\% attribution accuracy under 20\% token deletion while preserving near-unwatermarked semantic fidelity, establishing a practical paradigm for fine-grained provenance.
